issue: #628 — the descriptor repoint's carried sign-off item: 'the deposit arm's ExUnits are not unconditional (l2_datum is unbounded); both arms' frontiers get measured and recorded post-regeneration'. Carried to the #617 sign-off checklist.
spec: GOAL_SPEC §5.3 and §5.5.3: the LedgerOutputCommitmentV1 descriptor is the sole utxos_root trie value, so validate_valid_deposit_transition and apply_l2_outputs both pay for descriptor derivation, and §3.3 fixes the execution basis they are judged at.
purpose: Post-regeneration ExUnits frontier for the two arms #628 repointed onto LedgerOutputCommitmentV1 plus the isolated §5.3 descriptor derivation they both pay for. Unlike version 1 of this artifact this is a GATE: every row is re-measured by scripts/verify-transition-trace-descriptor-exec-ledger-v1.mjs, every crossing is a bracket between adjacent MEASURED rows rather than an interpolation, and every arm-cost claim is a difference against a fixture-only baseline that the verifier recomputes.
note:
Three things about these numbers a reader has to hold at once.

FIRST, an Aiken `check` reading is a WHOLE-TEST reading: it charges the fixture the test builds in-process — MPF roots, canonical CBOR, tx-id hashing, the descriptor derivations the fixture itself needs — to the row alongside the code under measurement. Every `kind: "arm"` row here is therefore an UPPER BOUND on what its arm costs on chain and not the arm's own figure. That is the same convention the tree's other execution ledgers pin, but the transition-trace rows carry far more fixture cost than the small door-opening rows those ledgers record, which is why version 1 of this artifact could not answer the question it was written to answer.

SECOND, that is what the `kind: "baseline"` rows are for. Each is built by the SAME builder function as its arm — `deposit_parts`, `l2_no_op_parts`, `sized_output_cbor` — and consumes every field that builder produces, then stops short of the entrypoint. The `marginal` block below names each pair and the verifier recomputes the difference from the fresh readings. Those differences, not the raw rows, are what licenses an arm-cost claim.

THIRD, and this is the finding that changes the #628 sign-off summary: NET OF FIXTURE COST NEITHER REPOINTED ARM IS OVER THE BASIS. The L2 no-op arm reads 15,289,803 mem whole-test — 115.8% of the §3.3 memory basis — but its fixture-only twin reads 9,530,768, so the marginal cost of `validate_accepted_transaction_fault_proof` including `apply_l2_outputs` is 5,759,035 mem, 43.6% of the basis. The deposit arm's widest measured rung is 8,102,746 marginal mem at a 266-byte serialised `l2_datum`, 61.4% of the basis. The over-basis whole-test readings are real and are pinned here as `exceeds`, but what they measure is a test harness, not a validator.

What the crossings then mean is narrower than version 1 claimed. `deposit_arm_l2_datum_bytes` crosses between an ABSENT `l2_datum` and a one-byte one — that is, the whole-test reading crosses on datum PRESENCE, not on datum width; every wider rung up to 266 bytes adds under 720K MARGINAL mem on top (the marginal span across those rungs is 717,375; the whole-test span across the same rungs is larger, +1,533,414, because fixture growth is charged to the row as well). `descriptor_output_cbor_bytes` crosses between a 2,687-byte and a 2,753-byte canonical output. Version 1 published an INTERPOLATED crossing at ~1,680 output bytes for the same dimension; that figure is retired and deliberately absent here. It was drawn between two pinned golden vectors of different SHAPE — a 74-byte bare output and a 2,355-byte output with two policies, three assets, a 56-byte base address and a PlutusV3 reference script — so its slope folded shape cost into size cost and overstated it by about 40%. The verifier refuses to publish an interpolation on a dimension that has a measured crossing, which is the discipline that failure earns.

A fourth thing, measured rather than assumed: the `l2_datum` ladder has no `Some(#"")` rung because that rung cannot be built. An otherwise-canonical output whose inline datum is the empty byte string `#"40"` — canonical Plutus data by `is_canonical_plutus_data_v1` — has NO §5.3 descriptor: `ledger_value_v1` returns `None` and every caller's `expect Some(..)` aborts. The one-byte datum immediately above it derives normally. The behaviour is pinned as an assertion in `derivation_declines_an_empty_inline_datum`; whether it is CORRECT is a §5.3/§6.2 question this lane raises and does not settle. See `openQuestions`.

One procedural note carried from version 1: Aiken evaluates a module's selected tests in parallel and `run-focused-check.mjs` puts every selector it is handed into one process, so each module is measured in its own invocation.
readingKind: Whole-test upper bounds. See `note`, paragraphs one and two: no raw row on this lane is a validator cost, and the `marginal` block is the only place an arm cost is stated.

compiler.why: The patched fork, not stock v1.1.22: the stock compiler that ships the blueprint has a live unsound codegen bug, so a reading taken with it would not be a reading of the code this tree ships.

blueprint.note: The blueprint is not an input to an `aiken check` reading; it is recorded so the reading is bound to the same regenerated source tree the #617 wave signs off. The two measurement modules this lane adds are test modules and move it by zero bytes.

measurement.harness: Every reading is taken through onchain/aiken/scripts/run-focused-check.mjs via exec-ledger-measure-v1.mjs, the repo's mandated reading path: it asserts the collected module is the one asked for and that every selected test passed, so a row for a test that did not run — or one that did not pass — cannot appear here. No reading was taken by spawning Aiken directly.
measurement.environment: MIDGARD_AIKEN_ENV=testnet. `env/default.ak` and `env/testnet.ak` differ only in `shift_duration` (30 against 3,600,000), which at least one pinned row here — `accepts_out_of_window_deposit_fault` — is sensitive to, so the verifier must be run with the same environment or its readings are readings of a different program. Every command below carries it.
measurement.memoryCap: Every measurement run was taken under `ulimit -v 16777216`. No run approached it: the widest peaked at 740,100 KB resident.
measurement.slotDiscipline: One `aiken` process machine-wide; every run in this lane waited on `pgrep -c -x aiken` reaching 0 before starting.
measurement.determinism: The descriptor rows were taken twice in two separate invocations and reproduced to the unit.
measurement.reproductionFidelity: The two sweep modules rebuild the fixtures of `accepts_valid_deposit_transition_fault` and `accepts_valid_l2_transaction_no_op_transition_fault` rather than importing them (a private `fn` in a `.test` module is not importable). The reproduction is faithful to within the record wrapper the sweep adds: `deposit_arm_datum_absent` reads 12,791,247 against the original's 12,776,094 (+15,153 mem, 0.12%) and `l2_no_op_arm` reads 15,289,803 against 15,279,779 (+10,024, 0.07%). Both originals are pinned as rows here, so the two can never drift apart unnoticed.

basis.source: GOAL_SPEC §3.3, as exported by GOAL_SPEC_EXECUTION_BASIS_V1 in onchain/aiken/scripts/exec-ledger-within-basis-v1.mjs — 20% margin off the supported L1 floor MIDGARD_CONSENSUS_LIMITS_V1.minSupportedL1MaxTxMemoryUnits of 16,500,000 mem. The verifier reads the basis from that module and never from this file.
basis.retiredFigure: #628's original note compared against an 11.2M reserve ceiling. That figure is retired; every judgement in this artifact is made at the §3.3 basis above.

modules.neutralisationNote: A cost row over a derivation that accepts anything measures nothing. These four selectors run in the same invocation as every row: the payload builder produces exact widths, the derivation refuses truncated bytes, it binds the output index it is salted with, and it declines an empty inline datum (the observation in `note` paragraph four).

descriptor_2753_bytes_derives.infeasibility: A single canonical output of 2,753 CBOR bytes cannot have its §5.3 descriptor derived inside the §3.3 memory basis by a whole test: the reading is 13,253,008 mem against a 13,200,000 basis. Net of its fixture-only twin the derivation itself still fits (13,125,202); the first rung where even the marginal derivation does not is 2,819 bytes.
descriptor_2753_bytes_derives.ruling: #628 sign-off item, #617 wave. No spec erratum is owed unless §5.3 is read as promising derivation for every L1-admissible output size; the owner ruling that settles that reading is not written yet.

descriptor_2819_bytes_derives.infeasibility: 2,819 CBOR bytes is the narrowest measured output whose descriptor derivation exceeds the basis NET of fixture cost as well as whole-test: 13,320,813 marginal mem against a 13,200,000 basis. descriptor_2819_bytes_derives.ruling: #628 sign-off item, #617 wave; same open reading of §5.3 as the row above.

descriptor_3083_bytes_derives.infeasibility: The widest rung measured, 3,083 CBOR bytes, at 14,231,781 mem whole-test and 14,103,335 marginal — 107.8% and 106.8% of the basis. descriptor_3083_bytes_derives.ruling: #628 sign-off item, #617 wave; same open reading of §5.3 as the two rows above.

crossings.claim: The deposit arm's whole-test reading crosses the §3.3 memory basis on l2_datum PRESENCE, between an absent datum and a one-byte one

What #628 asked — where does the unbounded l2_datum take the deposit arm over the basis — has the answer 'at the first byte, on the whole-test reading'. But the same ladder shows the answer is an artefact of the harness: the marginal cost at one byte is 7,385,371 mem and at 266 bytes it is 8,102,746, both comfortably within the basis. The width-driven part of the curve is about 2,900 mem per serialised datum byte, roughly 700K across the whole ladder, against a 1,644,852 step for presence alone.

openQuestions.question: An otherwise-canonical output whose inline datum is the empty byte string `#"40"` has no §5.3 descriptor: `ledger_value_v1` returns `None`, so `apply_l2_outputs` and `validate_valid_deposit_transition` abort on it rather than declining. `is_canonical_plutus_data_v1` accepts `#"40"` as canonical Plutus data and a one-byte datum derives normally, so the decline is not a canonicity rule at the datum level. Is an L2 output carrying an empty inline datum meant to be inadmissible to `utxos_root`, or is this a gap in the descriptor pipeline?
openQuestions.measuredHere: Yes — pinned by `derivation_declines_an_empty_inline_datum` in `midgard/ledger_output_descriptor_v1_exunits_frontier.test`. The cause was not localised in this lane; the decline is somewhere between `decode_canonical_output`, `ledger_output_summaries_v1` and `descriptor_is_well_formed`.
openQuestions.owner: Not settled here. Raised to the #617 wave orchestrator; this lane changed no validator code.

openQuestions.question: Descriptor derivation for a single canonical output stops fitting the §3.3 basis, net of all fixture cost, at 2,819 output CBOR bytes. Does §5.3 owe an explicit maximum serviceable output width, and must the L2 ledger refuse to admit an output the fraud-proof arms cannot re-derive? An output the ledger accepts but no fraud proof can re-derive is a hole in the same shape as the one #628 closed.
openQuestions.measuredHere: Yes — the `crossings` and `marginal` blocks bracket it between 2,753 and 2,819 bytes net of fixture, and between 2,687 and 2,753 whole-test.

openQuestions.question: #628 flagged `l2_datum` as unbounded. Measured, the deposit arm's marginal cost rises about 2,900 mem per serialised datum byte from 7,385,371 at one byte, so on this curve it would not reach the basis until roughly 1.9 KB — but the arm shares its budget with the rest of the fraud-proof transaction. Does §5.3 owe an explicit `l2_datum` width bound, or does the L1 transaction size limit bound it adequately?
openQuestions.measuredHere: Partly — the ladder runs to 266 serialised bytes and the slope past that is an extrapolation this ledger deliberately does not publish.

notMeasuredHere: Any output wider than 3,083 CBOR bytes, or any l2_datum wider than 266 serialised bytes. Both ladders stop where the curve is linear and a wider rung would add evidence but no new fact; nothing here extrapolates past them.

A fixture-only twin for `builds_rich_multi_chunk_output_exactly`, `l2_descriptor_dispute_over_a_descriptor_ledger_mints` or `rejects_l2_transaction_when_trace_matches_expected_post_root`. Those are pinned rows from version 1 rather than swept rungs; their marginal cost is read off the corresponding ladder instead.
The cause of the empty-inline-datum decline, and any change to it. This lane touched no validator code, no consensus pin and no pre-existing verifier.

Any change to the CG1 exclusion in docs/exec-plans/evidence/canonical-v1-cg1-control-publication-fit-v1.json. The re-measurement recorded there under `openItems[0].remeasured` shows the excluded resolver now fits with a +10,400-byte margin, but the exclusion itself is owner-owned and was left exactly as pinned.

adjacentMinorsVerifiedAtHead.detail: bdcb7d16 rewrote the it.each block formerly titled 'preserves the Aiken tag-4 output encoding for $label' into 'refuses to replay $label, which has no canonical ledger value'. The old body asserted that detectTransitionTraceFaults produced no l2_transaction_transition_matches_authenticated_replay detection for those shapes — i.e. that the tag-4 encoder round-tripped them byte for byte. The new body asserts a missingWitnessData rejection instead. adjacentMinorsVerifiedAtHead.detail: ledgerTrieValue wraps buildCanonicalMidgardLedgerEntryOutputMaterialV1 in a bare try/catch that returns the raw output bytes on any throw. Its comment justifies this for fixtures that deliberately feed non-canonical outputs, which have no descriptor. The catch is untyped and unconditional, so a genuine regression in the descriptor encoder — for any fixture, not just the deliberately-malformed ones — silently rebuilds the fixture's utxos_root from full output bytes, which is exactly the pre-#628 shape the repoint removed, and the suite can still go green over it.
